lessons.title: Declaring Rent to Your Employer: Form 124 and Proof Submission

body.text: Your employer can only give you an HRA exemption you have told them about and proved in the way they ask. Get the declaration and proofs in on time and the saving arrives in every monthly salary. Miss them and it arrives as a refund, a year or more later.

children.text: HRA exemption shows up in your take-home pay through TDS on salary under Section 392 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 192 of the 1961 Act). Your employer estimates your tax for the whole year and deducts it month by month. Whether that estimate includes your HRA exemption depends entirely on two things you control: the rent you declare, and the proof you submit.

markDefs.definition: The statement of claims an employee gives their employer under Section 392(5)(b) of the Income-tax Act, 2025, read with Rule 205 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026, so that TDS on salary can account for HRA, LTC, home loan interest and deductions. It replaced Form 12BB from 1 April 2026.

children.text: is the statement of claims you give your employer under Section 392(5)(b) of the Income-tax Act, 2025, read with Rule 205 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026. It replaced Form 12BB from tax year 2026-27. You give it to your employer, usually through the HR or payroll portal. It is not filed on the income tax portal.

cells: Part A
Your details: name, address, designation, PAN, employer and tax year
Part B: House Rent Allowance
Rent paid, landlord's name and address, landlord's PAN if annual rent exceeds ₹1,00,000, and your relationship with the landlord
Part B: Leave Travel Concession
Travel details and tickets or invoices
Part B: Interest on home loan
Interest paid, and the lender's name, address and PAN
Part B: Other deductions
Investments and payments such as PF, life insurance, ELSS, health insurance and NPS, with evidence

body.text: The relationship field is the biggest change from Form 12BB for HRA. Whatever you enter, parent, spouse, other relative or none, becomes part of the record your employer holds and can be matched with your landlord's PAN. Fill it in accurately. Lessons 9 and 11 cover what a genuine arrangement with a relative looks like.

body.title: How HRA moves through your salary in tax year 2026-27

events.title: Choose your regime and declare your rent
events.description: Tell your employer you want the old regime, then declare your expected rent and landlord details on the HR portal. Without this, TDS assumes the new regime and no HRA exemption.

events.title: Provisional TDS
events.description: Your employer deducts TDS each month assuming your declared rent is correct. Update the declaration if your rent, landlord or city changes.

events.title: Proof submission window
events.description: Submit Form 124 with rent receipts, the rent agreement and landlord PAN. Many employers also ask for bank statements. Deadlines are set by each employer.

events.title: Final TDS adjustment
events.description: Payroll replaces declared figures with proven figures. Any exemption you declared but did not prove is reversed, and the extra tax is recovered from your last salaries.

events.title: Form 130 issued
events.description: Your employer issues your salary TDS certificate, which replaced Form 16. It shows the HRA exemption your employer allowed.

events.title: File your return
events.description: Claim the correct exemption in your return, even if your employer did not allow it, and choose the old regime in the return.

children.text: What Happens When Proofs Are Missing

Pooja works in Hyderabad on a basic salary of ₹1,00,000 and HRA of ₹50,000 a month, and pays ₹40,000 a month in rent. She is on the old regime in the 30% slab. Her exempt HRA is the smallest of ₹6,00,000, ₹4,80,000 minus ₹1,20,000 = ₹3,60,000, and ₹6,00,000, so ₹3,60,000. That exemption reduces her annual tax by ₹1,12,320, or ₹9,360 a month.

Pooja declared her rent in April but was travelling in January and missed her employer's 31 January proof deadline. Payroll had given her the exemption from April to January. In February, it reversed the whole year's exemption and split the recovery across her last two salaries.

body.title: Extra TDS in Pooja's salary after missing the proof deadline
Show me the math behind the February and March hit

children.text: From April to January, TDS assumed the exemption, so each of those 10 months had ₹9,360 less TDS than it should have without proofs: ₹93,600 under-deducted in total. In February and March, two things happen. First, those months are taxed without the exemption, adding ₹9,360 each. Second, the ₹93,600 shortfall is recovered in two equal parts of ₹46,800. Together that is ₹56,160 of extra TDS in each of February and March, ₹1,12,320 in total, which is exactly the tax effect of the exemption for the whole year.
Payroll systems differ in how they spread a recovery, so the exact monthly split will vary. The total is the same.

stats.label: Tax she really owes on HRA
stats.context: Her rent is genuine, so she can claim it back in her return

body.text: Missing the employer's deadline does not cost you the exemption itself. You can still claim it in your return and get the excess TDS back as a refund. But the money sits with the government until your return is processed, which can be well after the July filing date. For Pooja, that is over ₹1.1 lakh of her own salary waiting several months.

body.title: Quick Check: After the Deadline
body.question: Rohan missed his employer's proof submission deadline, and his Form 130 shows no HRA exemption. His rent is genuine and documented. What should he do?
options: Nothing, because the exemption is lost for the year
Ask his employer to revise Form 130 in June
Claim the HRA exemption in his income tax return under the old regime and get the excess TDS refunded
Wait and claim double the exemption next year
body.explanation: The employer's deadline only affects TDS. Rohan's entitlement to the exemption comes from the law, not from Form 130. He can claim it in his return, keep his documents ready in case of questions, and receive the excess TDS as a refund. Lesson 15 walks through how.

body.title: Declaring in April vs claiming only in your return

columns.label: Declared in April, proved in January
points: TDS is ₹9,360 lower every month for Pooja
Take-home pay reflects the exemption all year
Return is simpler and mismatches with Form 130 are avoided

columns.label: Not declared at all
points: Exemption claimed only in the return
Refund arrives after processing, and the return differs from Form 130, which can prompt questions

body.title: Try It: The Monthly Difference
body.prompt: Aman expects an HRA exemption of ₹2,40,000 for the year and his income stays in the 20% slab under the old regime. By how much does declaring his rent to his employer reduce his TDS each month, including 4% cess? Answer in rupees.
body.explanation: Annual tax effect: ₹2,40,000 × 20% × 1.04 = ₹49,920. Spread over 12 months, that is ₹4,160 a month more in take-home pay, instead of a refund after he files his return.

body.caption: Keeping your declaration up to date
headers: What to do with your employer

cells: Rent increases at renewal
Update the declared rent from the month it changes and give the new agreement
You move flats or cities
Update the landlord details, address and city from the date you move, since the 50% or 40% limit may change
You join mid-year
Give Form 122 with your previous employer's salary and TDS, and Form 124 with your rent from your joining date
You move into your own home
Stop the HRA declaration from the month you move, so TDS is correct for the rest of the year
Your landlord has no PAN and rent exceeds ₹1,00,000
Ask HR how they want this documented before the deadline, not after
You declared the old regime but may switch to the new one
Your declaration only drives TDS. You can still choose the regime in your return

body.title: Scenario: Declared, Never Paid
body.scenario: Kunal declares ₹30,000 a month rent on his HR portal in April, naming a friend as landlord, to lower his TDS. He actually lives with his parents and pays nothing. When proof time comes, he submits nothing, planning to "sort it out in the return".
body.prompt: What happens at the employer, and what are his options when he files?
body.modelAnswer: From April to January, Kunal enjoys lower TDS based on a false declaration. When no proofs arrive, payroll reverses the exemption and recovers the tax from his February and March salaries, so his TDS catches up. At filing time, the honest position is to claim no HRA exemption, since he pays no rent. If he claims it in his return anyway, with his friend's PAN, he is making a false claim that can be exposed when his friend's return shows no rental income, leading to tax, interest and a penalty for misreporting. A declaration on an HR portal is not a free option. It should only ever reflect rent you actually pay.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: The Legal Basis
body.textWithBlank: Form 124 is given to your employer under Section ___(5)(b) of the Income-tax Act, 2025, the provision on TDS from salary.
body.explanation: Section 392 governs TDS on salary under the new Act, replacing Section 192 of the 1961 Act. Sub-section (5)(b) requires the employer to obtain evidence of claims, which is what Form 124 provides.

body.title: Form 124 Preparation Checklist
steps: In April, confirm your regime choice for the year on the HR portal
Declare your monthly rent, landlord name, address, PAN if annual rent exceeds ₹1,00,000, and relationship
Note your employer's proof submission deadline in your calendar with a reminder two weeks earlier
Collect monthly signed receipts and keep bank or UPI records of every rent payment
Upload Form 124 with the agreement, receipts and landlord PAN before the deadline
After March, check that Form 130 shows the HRA exemption you expected
If it does not, keep your documents ready to claim the exemption in your return

cards.definition: Statement of claims given to your employer under Section 392(5)(b) read with Rule 205 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026. Replaced Form 12BB. Not filed on the tax portal.
The rent and deductions you declare at the start of the year, used by your employer to estimate monthly TDS until proofs are submitted.
Submitting Form 124 with evidence, usually between December and January, so the employer can finalise TDS.
The extra tax recovered from the last months' salaries when declared exemptions are not proved.
The salary TDS certificate that replaced Form 16. It shows the HRA exemption your employer allowed.

points: Your employer applies HRA exemption in monthly TDS only if you declare your rent and later prove it
Form 124, given under Section 392(5)(b) and Rule 205, replaced Form 12BB and asks for landlord PAN above ₹1,00,000 and your relationship with the landlord
Declare rent in April and update it whenever rent, landlord or city changes
Missing the proof deadline triggers a TDS catch-up in February and March, but not a loss of the exemption itself
You can still claim a genuine exemption in your return and receive the excess TDS as a refund
Never declare rent you do not pay. The declaration is reversed at proof time and a false claim in your return can attract penalties
